_metadata.rubric: owner-clarified rubric with calibration anchors + no-literal-false-facts reminder, 2026-10-18
_metadata.independence: I read only u27-blind-input.json and no other file, repository search, web source or API.

hints.reason: LIGHT: lights glow; SHARK: only via the true but little-known fact that some deep-sea sharks are bioluminescent, which most players will not reach.
LIGHT: a lantern is a light; SHARK: the real lanternshark compound, accurate but niche.

best_available.why: It names a real shark (lanternshark) and is plainly a light, so it is the only hint with a concrete compound route to SHARK.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; both routes depend on deep-sea shark trivia.

hints.reason: LIGHT: basking in the light / sunlight; SNAKE: the familiar scene of a snake basking on a warm rock.
SNAKE: snakes have scales; LIGHT: only an invented route (weighing something light on a scale), so it is effectively one-sided.
LIGHT: sunlight; SNAKE: the familiar sunning-snake scene, moderate strength like TREAT for APPLE+HORSE.

best_available.why: Basking is strongly tied to snakes and naturally collocates with light/sunlight.

pairs.pair_note: BASK and SUN rely on the same sunning scene; SCALE does not reach LIGHT.

hints.reason: SPIDER: spider web; LIGHT: no familiar compound or scene links web to light.
LIGHT: porch light compound; SPIDER: the familiar scene of spiders webbing around the porch light where bugs gather.

best_available.why: Porch light is a solid compound and spiders around the porch light is a recognizable scene.

pairs.pair_note: Single moderate PASS.

hints.reason: LIGHT: daylight compound; SPRING: the familiar phrase spring day, with daylight saving starting in spring as a bonus.
SPRING: clock springs and 'spring forward'; LIGHT: only indirectly via daylight saving, which the word clock does not itself signal.
LIGHT: light bulb compound; SPRING: spring bulbs (tulips, daffodils) are a familiar gardening scene.

best_available.why: Two clean, familiar routes: light bulb and spring-flowering bulbs.

pairs.pair_note: BULB is excellent; DAY is a fair second.

hints.reason: LIGHT: lights shine; STAR: stars shine, a shared property.
LIGHT: light-year compound; STAR: only because light-years measure distances to stars, with no direct star-year phrase.
STAR: 'Twinkle, twinkle, little star'; LIGHT: twinkling fairy/holiday lights.

best_available.why: The nursery rhyme makes STAR unmistakable and twinkle lights reach LIGHT.

pairs.pair_note: Easy pair; YEAR leans on LIGHT.

hints.reason: LIGHT: signal lights; TRAIN: railway signals, one shared scene.
LIGHT: 'light at the end of the tunnel'; TRAIN: trains running through tunnels (and the oncoming-train joke).
LIGHT: light rail compound, itself a train system; TRAIN: trains run on rails.

best_available.why: Light rail is a compound that is literally a kind of train.

pairs.pair_note: Three solid PASSes.

hints.reason: WATER: sparkling water; LIGHT: light sparkles, and sunlight sparkling on water is one scene.
Rainbows are sunlight refracted through water droplets, a true shared phenomenon reaching both.
LIGHT: light reflection; WATER: reflections in water.

best_available.why: Directly physical for light and the classic image for water.

pairs.pair_note: Strong pair, no issues.

hints.reason: WITCH: Glinda the Good Witch; LIGHT: only via her glowing bubble or 'good = light' framing, which is thin.
WITCH: witches' wands; LIGHT: only via wand-lighting spells (e.g. Lumos) or glow wands, not a firm route.
LIGHT: candlelight; WITCH: the familiar witch scene of candles at spells and rituals (e.g. Hocus Pocus), moderate.

best_available.why: Candlelight is solid and candles are a stock prop of witch scenes.

pairs.pair_note: Moderate pair; GLINDA and WAND lean on WITCH.

hints.reason: WOLF: glowing wolf eyes in the dark; LIGHT: eyes reflecting/seeing light, a loose link on both sides.
LIGHT: moonlight; WOLF: the familiar (folkloric) image of a wolf howling at the moon.

best_available.why: Moonlight plus the iconic howling-wolf image.

pairs.pair_note: Wolf-howling-at-the-moon is a cultural image, not a behavioural fact; fine as a scene.

hints.reason: LION: lions roar; MOON: no route.
MOON: the moon at night; LION: only loosely via lions hunting at night or 'The Lion Sleeps Tonight', weak.

best_available.why: At least touches LION via nocturnal hunting; ROAR misses MOON entirely.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; needs a better hint.

hints.reason: Both via the fable 'The Lion and the Mouse'.
Both via Aesop's 'The Lion and the Mouse'.
The thorn belongs to Androcles and the Lion; in 'The Lion and the Mouse' the mouse gnaws through a net, so the MOUSE route is a wrong fact.

best_available.why: Points precisely at the one story containing both.

pairs.pair_note: THORN conflates two stories.

hints.reason: Contains NIGHT as a substring (rule failure), even though 'The Lion Sleeps Tonight' would reach both.
LION: 'The Lion Sleeps Tonight'; NIGHT: sleeping at night, inflected verb.
Via Lion King's 'Can You Feel the Love Tonight', but love alone reaches neither lion nor night clearly.

best_available.why: The song title makes both sides clear without containing a target.

pairs.pair_note: TONIGHT is a hard rule fail.

hints.reason: LION: the lion's mane; OCEAN: only via the lion's mane jellyfish, a real but niche ocean animal.
LION: sea lion compound; OCEAN: sea is a near-synonym, so it is very easy but valid.
LION: lionfish compound; OCEAN: fish live in the ocean (lionfish included).

best_available.why: Lionfish is a clean compound and an ocean animal, without leaning on a synonym.

pairs.pair_note: SEA works but is near-synonymous with OCEAN.

hints.reason: PIRATE: the Jolly Roger pirate flag; LION: only via lions on national/heraldic flags, a separate weak route.
LION: lions roar; PIRATE: pirates say 'arr', they are not known for roaring.

best_available.why: It reaches PIRATE strongly and LION at least through heraldry.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; needs a better hint.

hints.reason: Both via royal heraldry: lions on the royal arms/crest associated with the Queen, moderate strength.
Contains LION as a substring (rule failure).
LION: Nala is a lioness in The Lion King; QUEEN: she becomes Simba's queen.
LION: a lion pride; QUEEN: only via a stretched 'queen of the pride' or drag-queen/Pride link, not clear.

best_available.why: Names a lion who is a queen in the best-known lion story.

pairs.pair_note: LIONESS is a rule failure; the rest are moderate.

hints.reason: LION: lion tamer; RING: the tamer works in the circus ring.
LION: the circus lion jumping through a hoop; RING: a hoop is a ring shape (near-synonym).
LION: circus lions; RING: the circus ring / three-ring circus.

best_available.why: One scene containing both the lion and the ring.

pairs.pair_note: All three share the circus scene.

hints.reason: ROBOT: robots are mechanical; LION: no familiar route (mechanical lions are obscure).
Voltron is a giant robot formed from five robot lions, reaching both directly.

best_available.why: The only hint that touches LION, and it nails both.

pairs.pair_note: VOLTRON depends on cartoon familiarity; generation-dependent.

hints.reason: LION: Simba the lion; ROCK: Simba presented on Pride Rock.
LION: a pride of lions; ROCK: Pride Rock compound.

best_available.why: Lion pride and Pride Rock both land directly.

pairs.pair_note: Lion King carries the pair.

hints.reason: ROSE: the enchanted rose in Beauty and the Beast; LION: the lion as king of beasts.
LION: the Three Lions emblem; ROSE: the Tudor/English rose, both national symbols of England.

best_available.why: Both are national emblems of England, a single shared route.

pairs.pair_note: ENGLAND is moderately known outside the UK but widely recognisable via football.

hints.reason: SALT: salt lick; LION: no familiar lion-lick route.
LION: sea lion compound; SALT: sea salt compound.

best_available.why: Two clean compounds: sea lion and sea salt.

pairs.pair_note: Single strong PASS.

hints.reason: LION: The Lion King; SHADOW: only via the film's shadowy lands or the niche 'Shadow King', weak.
LION: Scar the Lion King villain; SHADOW: only via him living in his brother's shadow or the shadowlands, a stretch.

best_available.why: The dark villain living in Mufasa's shadow is the more evocative of two weak Lion King routes.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; both lean on LION.

hints.reason: Shared property: both are famous for big sharp teeth.
LION: king of the jungle / Lion King; SHARK: only a loose 'king of the sea' idea, not a set phrase.
Shared property: both are classic apex predators.

best_available.why: Captures both animals' defining shared role.

pairs.pair_note: Solid pair.

hints.reason: SNAKE: Kaa the python from The Jungle Book; LION: The Jungle Book has a tiger (Shere Khan), not a lion, so no route.
LION: 'king of the jungle' phrase; SNAKE: snakes in the jungle.

best_available.why: A familiar phrase for LION and a natural habitat for SNAKE.

pairs.pair_note: JUNGLE works as a phrase even though real lions live on savanna.

hints.reason: Contains LION as a substring (rule failure).
Shared property: lions hunt prey and many spiders are active hunters (e.g. huntsman spider), moderate.

best_available.why: The only rule-compliant hint; a fair shared-property route.

pairs.pair_note: HUNTER is broad but defensible like SWEET for APPLE+HONEY.

hints.reason: LION: lions leap on prey; SPRING: to spring is to leap (verb route).
LION: a lion pounces; SPRING: to spring on prey (verb route).
LION: 'in like a lion, out like a lamb'; SPRING: March begins spring.

best_available.why: The proverb ties March to lions and March is the start of spring.

pairs.pair_note: LEAP and POUNCE are the same verb route.

hints.reason: STAR: constellations are star patterns; LION: Leo is the lion constellation, moderate.
LION: Leo the lion; STAR: Leo star sign / constellation.
LION: Mufasa the Lion King; STAR: his speech that the great kings look down from the stars.

best_available.why: Leo is both the lion and a star sign/constellation.

pairs.pair_note: Strong pair.

hints.reason: LION: circus lions; TRAIN: the circus train (e.g. Dumbo).
LION: lion tamer; TRAIN: a tamer trains animals (verb route).

best_available.why: Circus train and circus lions share one scene.

pairs.pair_note: Good pair.

hints.reason: LION: sea lion; WATER: sea water.
WATER: water hole; LION: the savanna scene of lions at the water hole.
WATER: fountains spout water; LION: lion-head fountains are a familiar sight.

best_available.why: Sea lion and sea water are both direct.

pairs.pair_note: Three PASSes.

hints.reason: LION: lions roar; WOLF: wolves howl, they do not roar.
Shared property: both are top predators.
WOLF: wolf pack; LION: lions live in prides, not packs, so no route.

best_available.why: The only hint reaching both animals.

pairs.pair_note: ROAR and PACK are one-sided.

hints.reason: MOON: the book Goodnight Moon; MOUSE: the little mouse hidden on its pages, familiar to readers of the book.
MOON: the folk joke that the moon is made of cheese; MOUSE: mice love cheese.

best_available.why: Two famous cultural associations meeting in one word.

pairs.pair_note: GOODNIGHT's MOUSE side needs knowledge of the book.

hints.reason: MOON: full moon; NIGHT: only weakly via 'full night' or full-moon nights.
NIGHT: night sky; MOON: the moon in the sky.
MOON: moonlight; NIGHT: night light, both compounds.

best_available.why: Two clean compounds: moonlight and night light.

pairs.pair_note: Easy pair.

hints.reason: MOON: crescent moon; PIRATE: no familiar route.
PIRATE: pirates sail; MOON: only a vague sailing-by-moonlight or sailing-to-the-moon image.

best_available.why: Strong on PIRATE and at least gestures at moonlit sailing.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; needs a better hint.

hints.reason: MOON: the moon at night; QUEEN: the familiar phrase 'Queen of the Night' (Magic Flute aria, night-blooming flower).
MOON: Sailor Moon; QUEEN: only via the series' Queen Serenity lore, niche.

best_available.why: Queen of the Night is a recognised phrase and night pairs naturally with the moon.

pairs.pair_note: NIGHT is a moderate PASS; this is a judgement call.

hints.reason: Shared property: planets have moons and some have rings.
Saturn is famous for its rings and has many moons (e.g. Titan).
MOON: the real halo/ring around the moon; RING: a halo is a ring of light.

best_available.why: The single object most associated with both rings and moons.

pairs.pair_note: Strong pair.

hints.reason: MOON: the moon in space; ROBOT: robots and probes exploring space, moderate.
MOON: lunar rovers (including robotic ones like Lunokhod/Yutu); ROBOT: rovers are robotic explorers.
MOON: moon landing; ROBOT: only indirectly via robotic landers, no clear robot-landing phrase.

best_available.why: A rover is a robot and the moon is a famous rover destination.

pairs.pair_note: Avoid implying the crewed Apollo rover was a robot; robotic lunar rovers do exist.

hints.reason: ROCK: meteors are space rocks; MOON: only via meteor impacts on the moon, which the word does not point at.
MOON: the Apollo landings; ROCK: Apollo brought back moon rocks.
MOON: lunar craters; ROCK: craters are rocky impact holes made by space rocks.

best_available.why: Moon rocks from the Apollo missions tie both directly.

pairs.pair_note: Good pair.

hints.reason: ROSE: roses fade; MOON: the moon fades at dawn; both are loose, poetic routes.
MOON: moonrise / the moon rises; ROSE: 'rose' is the past tense of rise (ordinary inflection).

best_available.why: A clever but fair inflection route plus moonrise.

pairs.pair_note: RISE is a nice wordplay hint.

hints.reason: SALT: sea salt; MOON: the moon pulls the sea's tides and its plains are called seas (Sea of Tranquility).
MOON: the moon drives tides; SALT: only indirectly via tidal salt water or salt marshes.

best_available.why: Sea salt is direct and the sea links to the moon by tides and lunar seas.

pairs.pair_note: Moderate pair.

hints.reason: MOON: the phrase 'dark side of the moon'; SHADOW: shadows are dark.
An eclipse involves the moon and a cast shadow (Earth's shadow on the moon or the moon's shadow on Earth).

best_available.why: Literally a moon-and-shadow event.

pairs.pair_note: 'Dark side of the moon' is a phrase, not a claim the far side is always dark.

hints.reason: MOON: the moon at night; SHARK: only via sharks hunting at night (or the niche night shark species).
MOON: the moon drives tides; SHARK: no familiar shark-tide route beyond both involving the ocean.

best_available.why: At least reaches SHARK through nocturnal hunting.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; needs a better hint.
